1.q: וַ⁠יְהִ֧י דְבַר יְהוָ֛ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ שֵׁנִ֑ית
1.note: Jeremiah is using the phrase translated as **And the word of Yahweh was to Jeremiah a second time** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.
See how you translated the similar expression in 28:12. This also occurs in verses 19 and 23.

Here Jeremiah is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

The expression **was still confined** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [while the guards were still holding him]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:4.
The term **saying** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this term explicitly.

2.note: The pronoun **its** refers to the earth, which Yahweh made and put in place. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the maker of the earth … forming it … to establish it]
Here, **to** marks **establish it** as the goal or purpose of **forming it**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose.
See how you translated the similar expression in 2:5.

3.note: The word translated as **Call** is an imperative, but it communicates a condition rather than a command. If the imperative does not communicate a condition for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates a condition. Alternate translation: [‘If you call to me, then I will answer you]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the things that people cannot discover on their own were **inaccessible things**, that is, fortified places that no one can enter. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and things you could not find out by yourself]

4.note: The expression **are torn down** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [that the people have torn down]

Here, **the sword** represents “warfare” that the enemy soldiers will wage against them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [warfare]
See how you translated the similar expression in 21:4.
See how you translated the similar expression in 21:11.
See how you translated the similar expression in 24:8.
See how you translated the similar expression in 26:13.

5.note: The pronoun **They** refers to the people of this city, who are going out to fight against the Chaldeans. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [The people of this city are coming]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **man**. He means the people of this city in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the corpses of the people]

The implication is that when Yahweh says that he will **strike** these people, he means that he will kill them. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [in my anger and in my wrath I will put to death]
See how you translated this expression in 7:20.

Yahweh is using **I have hidden my face from this city** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I have turned away from this city and refused to help it.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I have turned away from this city]
See how you translated the similar expression in 21:5.

6.note: The terms **healing** and **a cure** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [complete healing]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people of this city were sick people whom he would **heal** and **cure**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will restore them]
If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **peace** and **truth**, you could express the same ideas in another way as in the UST.
See how you translated the similar expression in 31:8. This also occurs in verse 14.
See how you translated the similar expression in 14:13.

7.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 29:14. This also occurs in verse 11 and 26.

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people of Judah and Israel were a building that he would **build**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will make them prosper again]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [as I built them at the first]

8.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the sin of the people, were dirty, from which he would **cleanse** them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will remove all their iniquity]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **iniquity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [from all their wicked deeds … all their wicked deeds]

9.q: וְ⁠הָ֣יְתָה לִּ֗⁠י & אֲשֶׁ֤ר אָֽנֹכִי֙ עֹשֶׂ֣ה אֹתָ֔⁠ם
9.note: The pronoun **it** refers to this city, Jerusalem. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And Jerusalem will be for me … that I am doing for the people of this city, Jerusalem]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **joy**, **praise**, and **glory**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [a name that causes people to rejoice, to praise me, and to honor me]

Here, **a name** represents “a reputation.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [a reputation that brings joy, praise, and glory]

Yahweh is using the adjective **good** as a noun to mean a certain kind of thing. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [everything good … everything good]

The terms **fear** and **tremble** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [And they will be overcome with awe]
See how you translated the similar expression in 13:11.

10.note: The expression **there will be heard** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Again you will hear]

10.q: אַתֶּ֣ם אֹֽמְרִ֔ים חָרֵ֣ב ה֔וּא מֵ⁠אֵ֥ין אָדָ֖ם וּ⁠מֵ⁠אֵ֣ין בְּהֵמָ֑ה
10.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as an indirect quotation. Alternate translation: [you are saying that it is a waste, without man and without beast]
See how you translated the similar expression in 4:25. This also occurs in verse 12.

11.q: ק֣וֹל שָׂשׂ֞וֹן וְ⁠ק֣וֹל שִׂמְחָ֗ה ק֣וֹל חָתָן֮ וְ⁠ק֣וֹל כַּלָּה֒
11.note: Here, **the voice** represents “the sounds that people make.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the sounds of joy and the sounds of gladness, the sounds of the bridegroom and the sounds of the bride, the sounds of]

11.q: ק֣וֹל אֹמְרִ֡ים הוֹדוּ֩ אֶת יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת כִּֽי ט֤וֹב יְהוָה֙ כִּֽי לְ⁠עוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּ֔⁠וֹ
11.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as an indirect quotation. Alternate translation: [the voice of the ones saying that people should give thanks to Yahweh of Armies, because Yahweh is good and his covenant faithfulness is forever,]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **covenant faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way as in the UST.
The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before.
See how you translated the similar phrase in Jeremiah 29:41.
See how you translated the similar expression in 7:34.
See how you translated the similar expression in 7:34.
See how you translated the similar expression in 17:26.

12.note: Yahweh is not distinguishing **this place** from another place that is **desolate**. He is reminding the people of Judah that Jerusalem and its surrounding towns are presently without people or animals, even as he promises that shepherds and their flocks will fill this land again. Be sure that this is clear in your translation. Alternate translation: [in this place, which currently lies in ruins,]

Yahweh is using the adjective **desolate** as a noun to mean a certain kind of place. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [the place that is desolate]
See how you translated the similar expression in 7:3.

13.note: Yahweh is using **will pass under the hands of the one counting** as a common expression of the culture to mean “will be counted one by one by their shepherd.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the sheep will each be counted by their shepherd]

14.note: See how you translated **days are coming** in 7:32.
See how you translated this expression in 5:11.
See how you translated the similar expression in 29:10.

15.note: See how you translated this same phrases in Jeremiah 23:5. Alternate translation: [a righteous heir]
See how you translated the similar expression in 22:3.

16.note: See how you translated this phrase in 23:6.

Here, **Jerusalem** represents “the people who live in Jerusalem.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and the people living in Jerusalem will dwell in security]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **security**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and Jerusalem will dwell securely]
See how you translated the similar expression in 23:6.

17.note: The expression **will not be cut off** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [David will never lack a man]

Yahweh is using **A man will not be cut off for** as a common expression of the culture to mean David “will never lack a male descendant.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [David will never lack a male descendant]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **man**. He means descendants of David in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [One of David’s descendants]
Here, **the throne** represents “ruling as king.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [ruling as king over]

18.note: The expression **will not be cut off** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I will never cut off a man from before my face]

Yahweh is using **a man will not be cut off** as a common expression of the culture to mean “there will always be a man.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [ever lack a man]

Here, **my face** represents “my presence.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. This also occurs in verse 24. Alternate translation: [from serving in my presence]
Yahweh is using **all the days** as a common expression of the culture to mean “forever” or “always.” See how you translated the this expression in 31:36. Alternate translation: [forever]

20.q: אִם־תָּפֵ֨רוּ֙ אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֣⁠י הַ⁠יּ֔וֹם וְ⁠אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֖⁠י הַ⁠לָּ֑יְלָה וּ⁠לְ⁠בִלְתִּ֛י הֱי֥וֹת יֽוֹמָם־וָ⁠לַ֖יְלָה בְּ⁠עִתָּֽ⁠ם & גַּם־בְּרִיתִ֤⁠י תֻפַר֙ אֶת־דָּוִ֣ד עַבְדִּ֔⁠י מִ⁠הְיֽוֹת־ל֥⁠וֹ בֵ֖ן מֹלֵ֣ךְ עַל־כִּסְא֑⁠וֹ וְ⁠אֶת־הַ⁠לְוִיִּ֥ם הַ⁠כֹּהֲנִ֖ים מְשָׁרְתָֽ⁠י
20.note: Yahweh is making a conditional statement that sounds hypothetical, but he knows that the condition is not true or possible. He is stating it as a condition to show that what he says in the following verse also is not true or possible. He means that just as the Judeans cannot **break** his **covenant of the day** and **covenant of the night** in order to keep **night and day** from coming **in their time**, so also his **covenant** with **David** and with the **priests** will never **be broken**. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that the speaker believes is not true. Alternate translation: [Just as it is impossible for you to break my covenant of the day and my covenant of the night, so that day and night do not come in their time, so also I will never break my covenant with my servant David that he will always have a son reigning on his throne and my covenant with the Levites, the priests, my ministers]
The pronoun **you** refers to the people of Judah, whom Yahweh is addressing. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [If you people of Judah break]

20.q: אֶת בְּרִיתִ֣⁠י הַ⁠יּ֔וֹם וְ⁠אֶת בְּרִיתִ֖⁠י הַ⁠לָּ֑יְלָה
20.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **covenant** that is characterized by his appointment of **the day** and **the night** to come at their proper times. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [my covenant that established the day and my covenant that established the night]

20.q: אֶת בְּרִיתִ֣⁠י הַ⁠יּ֔וֹם וְ⁠אֶת בְּרִיתִ֖⁠י הַ⁠לָּ֑יְלָה
20.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the fixed order by which day and night follow each other were a **covenant** that he had made. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my fixed order for the day and my fixed order for the night]

The words translated as **so that** indicate that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [Thus says Yahweh: ‘If you break my covenant of the day and my covenant of the night, with the result that day and night do not come in their time]

21.note: The expression **will be broken** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I will end my covenant]
Here, **his throne** represents ruling as king with royal authority If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language as in the UST.

22.q: אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא יִסָּפֵר֙ צְבָ֣א הַ⁠שָּׁמַ֔יִם וְ⁠לֹ֥א יִמַּ֖ד ח֣וֹל הַ⁠יָּ֑ם כֵּ֣ן אַרְבֶּ֗ה
22.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **the host of the heavens** and **the sand of the sea** are too many to number, so the descendants of David and the Levites will be too many to number. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [Just as the host of the heavens is too vast to count, and the sand of the sea is too much to measure, so I will vastly increase the number of]

22.q: לֹֽא יִסָּפֵר֙ צְבָ֣א הַ⁠שָּׁמַ֔יִם וְ⁠לֹ֥א יִמַּ֖ד ח֣וֹל הַ⁠יָּ֑ם
22.note: The expressions **be counted** and **be measured** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use those forms, you could express the ideas in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [no one can count the host of the heavens, and no one can measure the sand of the sea]
See how you translated the similar expression in 19:13.
See how you translated “seed” in 7:15 where it is used with the same meaning.

23.q: The word of Yahweh came to Jeremiah, saying,
23.note: This idiom is used to introduce a special message from God. See how you translated a similar phrase in Jeremiah 1:4. Alternate translation: [Yahweh gave a message to Jeremiah. He said,] or [Yahweh spoke this message to Jeremiah:]

24.q: הֲ⁠ל֣וֹא רָאִ֗יתָ מָֽה־הָ⁠עָ֤ם הַ⁠זֶּה֙ דִּבְּר֣וּ לֵ⁠אמֹ֔ר שְׁתֵּ֣י הַ⁠מִּשְׁפָּח֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֨ר בָּחַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה בָּ⁠הֶ֖ם וַ⁠יִּמְאָסֵ֑⁠ם
24.note: Yahweh is using the question form to call attention to what the people are saying. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You have certainly noticed what this people has spoken, saying, ‘The two families that Yahweh chose in them, now he has rejected them.’]

24.q: הֲ⁠ל֣וֹא רָאִ֗יתָ מָֽה־הָ⁠עָ֤ם הַ⁠זֶּה֙ דִּבְּר֣וּ לֵ⁠אמֹ֔ר שְׁתֵּ֣י הַ⁠מִּשְׁפָּח֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֨ר בָּחַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה בָּ⁠הֶ֖ם וַ⁠יִּמְאָסֵ֑⁠ם
24.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as an indirect quotation. Alternate translation: [Have you not seen what this people has spoken, saying that Yahweh has now rejected the two families that he had chosen]

The implication is that **The two families** are the kingdom of Israel and the kingdom of Judah. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [The two family lines, Israel and Judah,]

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **my people**, whom the people are despising, after the information about the despising. Alternate translation: [Thus they despise my people]

Here, **before their face** represents being in presence of them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before them]

25.q: אִם־לֹ֥א בְרִיתִ֖⁠י יוֹמָ֣ם וָ⁠לָ֑יְלָה חֻקּ֛וֹת שָׁמַ֥יִם וָ⁠אָ֖רֶץ לֹא־שָֽׂמְתִּי
25.note: Yahweh is speaking as if this were a hypothetical possibility, but he means that it is actually true that he has established the fixed order of day and night. If your language does not state something as a condition if it is certain or true, or if your readers might think that what Yahweh is saying is uncertain, then you could translate this as a confident statement. Alternate translation: [I have surely established my covenant of day and night, and I have surely set the statutes of heaven and earth]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the fixed order by which day and night follow each other were a **covenant** that he had established. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my fixed order for day and night]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **the statutes** that govern **heaven and earth**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the statutes that govern heaven and earth]

26.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about what Yahweh would do before the information about whom he would do it to. Alternate translation: [I will reject the seed of Jacob and David my servant]
See how you translated “seed” in 7:15 where it is used with the same meaning. Alternate translation: [the descendants of Jacob … from his descendants over the descendants of Abraham]
The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before.
See how you translated this same phrase in Jeremiah 29:14.
